main_text.p: ribus quæstionem τὴν ἔνεκεν Ἀπόστολος ὑ-πάρχων ὁ Παῦλος πρὸς τὰ ἔθνη, Ἑβραίους πιστέλ-λει; Unde Paulus, Gentium sanè Apostolus, ad Hebræos scribat?

XXVI. Eulogius Archiepiscopus Alexandrinus, florens sub Martiano Imperatore, medio quinto sæculo, ut ex Photij Bibliothecâ, in excerptis Eulogianis Cod. ccxxx; L. ii. Contrà Novatianos, apud eundem Photium Cod. cccxxx. respondens objectioni Novatianorum ex loco Hebr. vi.4. x. 24. τοὺς Φέρωσιν οἱ ἀπὸ Νοvατ-ιανοῦ τὴν Ἀποστολικὴν ῥῆσιν, τὸ Φάσκον. τῆς ἅπαξ φωτισθέντας &c. Proferunt Novatiani di-ctum Apostoli, docens, Impossibile &c. De eodem loco; φησὶν ὁ θεσπέσιος Παῦλος, dicit divus Paulus; οὕτως οὖν ἀφέντες τὴν τῆς Χριστοῦ διδασκαλίαν ὁ Παῦλος, ἐπὶ τὴν τε-λειότητα ἔρχεται. Sic ergo omittit elementa-lem illam doctrinam Paulus, & ad perfe-ctionem venit. Sic alia citaturus loca ex eodem Epistolio, λέγει ὁ Ἀπόστολος; ὡς αὐτὸς ὁ Ἀπόστολος φησί.

page.notes: The Greek is set in a small italic face and is only partly legible on the scan; the exact letters of the Greek words in the first and later lines are doubtful and should be checked against a better image. The Latin and Greek hyphenations are kept as printed. The bottom-right "XXVII" is a bare numeral at the foot and is recorded as a catchword, since it stands where a catchword would. The Latin word "Novatianus" split across a line end ("Novat-ιανοῦ") is a mixed Latin/Greek form in the print and may be misread.
